tagline: Over Galena Summit, from the Salmon watershed to the Big Wood
intro: The Sawtooth Scenic Byway follows Idaho 75 between Stanley and Shoshone, crossing Galena Summit between the Salmon and Big Wood river valleys. This two-lane highway runs through the Sawtooth Valley, with the Sawtooth Mountains to the west and the White Cloud Mountains farther east. The pass reaches 8,701 feet, with a viewpoint on its Stanley side overlooking the Salmon headwaters. The route provides access to the Sawtooth National Recreation Area. North of Ketchum, the highway passes its headquarters before climbing past Galena Lodge toward the summit.

The road dates to at least 1926, when it carried the U.S. 93 designation. In 1977, U.S. 93 moved to the former alternate route through Arco, and this road became State Highway 75. The overlook had opened in 1964; it was renamed for Frank and Bethine Church in 2006. Before the road became Idaho 75, the pass already carried travelers on U.S. 93.

Heading south from Stanley, pass the Redfish Lake turnoff and follow the Salmon valley toward Galena Summit. Beyond the pass, descend toward Ketchum beneath the Boulder Mountains, whose peaks rise above 11,000 feet. The Big Wood valley carries the highway through Hailey and Bellevue, then toward Shoshone, where the surrounding land includes extensive lava rock.

moments.title: Redfish Lake
moments.text: Redfish Lake takes its name from the sockeye salmon that returned here from the Pacific Ocean to spawn. The lake lies south of Stanley in the Sawtooth National Recreation Area. A paved road branches from Idaho 75 to its north shore. At the opposite end, Mount Heyburn and Grand Mogul frame the water. The lake extends 4.5 miles, but the trail around it runs 17.5 miles. Forest Service facilities support hiking, camping and water sports along the lake. The Forest Service developed the shore for recreation while largely maintaining the natural landscape of the surrounding Sawtooth Mountains.

moments.title: Galena Summit
moments.text: Galena Summit divides the Salmon River drainage from the Big Wood River drainage. The highway crosses at 8,701 feet in the Boulder Mountains. On the Stanley side, Galena Overlook stands a little more than a mile west of the summit, at 8,400 feet. Its view takes in the Sawtooth range and the Salmon headwaters. Opened in 1964, the overlook was renamed for Frank and Bethine Church in 2006 and renovated in 2010. The highway pass also carried a stage of the Women’s Challenge bicycle race, held from 1984 to 2002.

moments.title: Ketchum
moments.text: Ketchum began as a smelting center called Leadville in 1880. When mining declined in the 1890s, sheepmen drove flocks through town to summer grazing in the higher mountains. In autumn, the sheep returned to corrals at the Union Pacific railhead, connected to the main line at Shoshone. The town marks its wagon history each Labor Day weekend with Wagon Days, whose parade includes narrow ore wagons. Two streams, Trail Creek and Warm Springs Creek, join the Big Wood River in town. Ketchum and neighboring Sun Valley share the valley beneath Bald Mountain.

moments.title: Shoshone Ice Caves
moments.text: The Shoshone Ice Caves are lava tubes where ice remains frozen through summer. They lie about 15 miles north of Shoshone, in a region where lava rock covers much of the land. That rock also limits farmland and makes excavation for buildings difficult.
